title: What continuing education do pharmacists need in the US?
description: US pharmacist CE as at November 2026: ACPE credit rules, CPE Monitor and topic codes, and law, opioid and other mandates in California, Florida and Texas.
shortAnswer: US pharmacists renew their licenses through state boards of pharmacy, which set continuing education hours and mandatory topics, while the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE) accredits most providers and defines how credit is measured and reported. As at November 2026, California, Florida and Texas each require 30 hours every two years, with state specific law, controlled substance or opioid, medication error, cultural competency or human trafficking content inside those hours.
keyTakeaways: ACPE accredits continuing pharmacy education providers; for live activities 60 minutes equals one contact hour (0.1 CEU), and providers upload credit to CPE Monitor within 60 days.
Each ACPE activity carries a Universal Activity Number whose topic designator identifies law (03), patient safety (05) and opioids, pain management or substance use disorder (08) content.
California requires 30 hours in 24 months, including 2 hours of a board provided law and ethics course and 1 hour of cultural competency, and certificates kept four years.
Florida requires 30 hours in two years, including 2 hours on controlled substances and 2 hours on medication errors in the board's breakdown.
Texas requires 30 contact hours each license period, including 1 hour on Texas pharmacy law and an approved human trafficking course, with certificates kept three years.
jurisdiction: United States (ACPE accreditation; state boards of pharmacy in California, Florida and Texas)
regulator: Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE); California State Board of Pharmacy; Florida Board of Pharmacy; Texas State Board of Pharmacy
appliesTo: Licensed pharmacists renewing in California, Florida or Texas
Pharmacy employers, health system pharmacy departments and chains tracking pharmacist CE
ACPE accredited providers of continuing pharmacy education
Pharmacy technicians are subject to separate state rules not covered here

sections.heading: Who sets continuing education requirements for US pharmacists?

blocks.text: State boards of pharmacy set the hours, cycles and mandatory topics, through state pharmacy acts and board rules. ACPE does not set renewal hours for pharmacists; it accredits providers and sets standards for how continuing pharmacy education is designed, measured and reported, which most boards accept as the default route to approved credit.

The practical consequence is a two layer record. The provider's ACPE accreditation and activity number establish that a course is valid credit; the state rule decides whether it satisfies a particular topic mandate. Employers tracking pharmacists in several states need both layers, as in a [compliance obligations register](/glossary/compliance-obligations-register).

sections.heading: How does ACPE define and report pharmacy CE credit?

blocks.text: ACPE's [CPE Policies and Procedures Manual](https://www.acpe-accredit.org/wp-content/uploads/CPE-Policies-Procedures-Updated-January-2026_FINAL-1.pdf) sets the mechanics. For live activities, credit is based on real time: "60 minutes = one (1) contact hour (0.1 CEU)." Providers decide the credit for each activity in advance, and must offer and award ACPE credit to learners who complete content meeting ACPE's definition of continuing education.

Providers submit participant information through CPE Monitor, the electronic tracking service ACPE runs with the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy, within 60 days of the learner's participation. The manual states that the official record of credit is the learner's e-profile in CPE Monitor, not a paper certificate, and late uploads after 60 days carry a fee and a separate request process. Providers must review content at least once every three years.

Every activity has a Universal Activity Number (UAN) built from the provider number, a joint provider code, the year, a sequence number, a format letter (L for live, H for home study) and a topic designator, ending in P for pharmacists or T for technicians. ACPE's example is 0197-0000-22-001-L05-P.

blocks.text: California requires 30 hours of continuing education in the prior 24 months to renew a pharmacist license, under [California Code of Regulations, title 16, section 1732.5](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/16-CCR-1732.5), as amended with an operative date of July 29, 2024. At least 2 of the 30 hours must be a board provided course in law and ethics, and at least 1 hour must be a cultural competency course covering the content required by Business and Professions Code section 4231.

items: Pharmacists providing smoking cessation therapy: at least 1 hour on that topic.
Pharmacists providing travel medicine: at least 2 hours.
Pharmacists furnishing emergency contraception: at least 1 hour.
Pharmacists providing immunizations and vaccinations: at least 1 hour.
Pharmacists who prescribe any Schedule II controlled substance: at least 1 hour, once every four years, in a board approved course on the risks of addiction associated with Schedule II drugs.

blocks.text: All of these hours sit within the 30. Section 1732.5(e) requires all pharmacists to keep certificates of completion for four years after completing each course.

Florida requires not less than 30 hours of continuing professional pharmaceutical education in the two years before renewal, under [section 465.009, Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0465/Sections/0465.009.html). The Florida Board of Pharmacy's [pharmacist renewal page](https://floridaspharmacy.gov/pharmacist-renewal/) breaks the 30 into 26 general hours, which can be ACPE or board approved, 2 hours on controlled substances and 2 hours on medication errors, both board approved.

Pharmacists certified to administer vaccines or epinephrine autoinjection must complete a 3 hour course from a statewide physician association accredited for AMA PRA Category 1 credit, within the 30 hours. Collaborative practice certification adds an 8 hour board approved course, and test and treat certification a 3 hour course. New licensees renewing 12 months or more after licensure complete 15 hours including medication errors, controlled substances and 1 hour of HIV/AIDS.

Florida pharmacists also had to complete a one-time 1 hour human trafficking course by January 1, 2021 under section 456.0341, which covers pharmacists licensed under chapter 465. That duty, and the related workplace sign, are covered in [human trafficking training requirements for healthcare](/regulations/human-trafficking-training-requirements-healthcare).

Texas requires 30 contact hours (3.0 CEUs) of approved continuing education during the previous license period, under [22 Texas Administrative Code section 295.8](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/22-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-295-8) and section 559.053 of the Texas Pharmacy Act. Within the 30 hours, at least 1 contact hour must relate to Texas pharmacy laws or rules.

New pharmacists must complete at least 2 contact hours on approved procedures for prescribing and monitoring controlled substances, under Health and Safety Code section 481.07635, by the first anniversary of licensure. Every pharmacist must have completed the human trafficking prevention course required by Occupations Code section 116.002. Alternatives to hours include passing the NAPLEX during the license period, or one credit hour per license year in an ACPE accredited professional degree program.

A pharmacist who does not report the required hours is not renewed and, if practicing, is subject to the penalties for practicing without a license. Certificates must be kept for three years from the date the hours are reported on a renewal application, in paper or electronic form, and disallowed hours found in a board audit can lead to discipline.

sections.heading: How do the three states compare, and what evidence should employers hold?

blocks.text: All three states use 30 hours over a roughly two year period, but the mandated topics and retention periods differ. The table is an original mapping of each obligation to who it applies to, its frequency and the evidence a board auditor would expect, suited to a pharmacist [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix).

For setting the review dates, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can use ACPE topic designators as structured metadata, so a course coded 03 or 08 is matched to the state law and opioid obligations it may satisfy, while the state rule decides the final mapping. Retention periods, four years in California and three in Texas, attach to each certificate by jurisdiction. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Does ACPE set how many CE hours pharmacists need?
faqs.a: No. State boards of pharmacy set the hours and mandatory topics. ACPE accredits continuing pharmacy education providers and sets standards for credit, activity numbering and reporting through CPE Monitor, which most boards accept as evidence that a course is approved.

faqs.q: Is a paper certificate enough proof of ACPE credit?
faqs.a: ACPE's manual states that the official record of ACPE credit is the learner's e-profile in CPE Monitor. Providers must upload participant information within 60 days. State rules on retaining certificates still apply, such as four years in California and three years in Texas.

faqs.q: What does the topic code in an ACPE activity number mean?
faqs.a: It identifies the subject category. For example, 03 is law related to pharmacy practice, 05 is patient safety, 06 is immunizations and 08 is opioids, pain management and substance use disorder. A state may still require its own approval for a topic, such as Florida's board approved controlled substance and medication error courses.

faqs.q: Do pharmacists need live CE hours?
faqs.a: Some states set a minimum number of live hours. This page does not list live hour minimums because they were not confirmed on the board sources reviewed for California, Florida and Texas. Check the board rule directly before planning a cycle that relies entirely on home study.
